hints.S01_A1: The sentence compares the hall to a BEEHIVE, and tells you children were rushing everywhere with music playing. Ask: is a beehive famous for stillness, or for non-stop activity? Match the adjective to that picture.
hints.S01_A2: Look at what the puppy is doing: running around and CHASING a butterfly. Ask: does that action sound tired and gloomy, or full of energy and fun? The adverb must match the mood of the action.
hints.S01_A3: Mia STAYED behind on purpose, so the room would be ready before the next class arrived. Ask: would a helpful student damage the room, or leave it in good order? Pick the phrasal verb that helps rather than harms.
hints.S01_A4: The dash gives you the meaning: she JUMPED for joy. Ask: which idiom means extremely happy? The others describe being ill, in trouble, or confused - none of those make you jump.
hints.S01_A5: Priya RAISED her hand on purpose, even though the question was hard. Ask: would you volunteer in front of the class to give an answer you believed was wrong? Do not let the word DIFFICULT trick you into a length-based choice.
hints.S01_B1: Look at the subject: NOBODY. Words like nobody, everyone and somebody act like ONE person, even though they feel like many. Ask: does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the verb ending in -s?
hints.S01_B2: The helper verb HAS is already in the sentence. Ask: which verb form must follow have/has to build the present perfect? Not the base form, not the -ing form - you need the third form (the past participle).
hints.S01_B3: Two things happen here: one long action and one sudden one. The bell RANG is the sudden event that cuts in. Ask: which tense shows an action already in progress when something interrupts it?
hints.S01_B4: The word THAN is your signal - you are comparing exactly TWO libraries, not three or more. Ask: does comparing two things need the comparative or the superlative? And never stack 'more' in front of an -er ending.
hints.S01_B5: The sentence describes something that already happened, so that Mia COULD sit down. Ask: what is the past form of this verb? Careful - it is irregular, so adding -ed will not work.
hints.S01_B6: This is a question tag. The main clause is positive and its verb IS the 'to be' verb. Ask: does a positive statement take a positive tag or a negative one? The tag must also reuse the same verb from the statement.
hints.S01_B7: The helper DID not already carries the past tense for you. Ask: once a helper verb has shown the tense, what form does the main verb take? Do not mark the tense twice.
hints.S01_B8: The LIBRARIAN is speaking directly TO the students, not about herself or about other people. Ask: from the speaker's point of view, whose books are these? Match the possessive to the person being addressed.
hints.S01_C1: Ms Tan LED the whole class onto the bus - the writer is one of the people being led. Ask: which pronoun means 'me and the people with me' in the OBJECT position, after the verb? Not the doing form 'we'.
hints.S01_C2: The person doing the telling is MS TAN - one woman, and the pronoun starts the sentence, so it is the one acting. Ask: which pronoun is the SUBJECT form for a single female? The object form only comes after a verb or a preposition.
hints.S01_C3: The excited one is RAJU - one boy, and this pronoun starts the sentence, so it is doing the pointing. Ask: which pronoun is the SUBJECT form for one male? Not 'him', which comes after a verb.
hints.S01_C4: Ms Tan SMILED AT Raju - he is receiving the smile, and the pronoun comes after 'at'. Ask: which pronoun for one male goes AFTER a verb or preposition? The subject form cannot sit there.
hints.S01_C5: The NOTEBOOK belongs to RAJU. Ask: which word shows that something belongs to one male? Careful: two of the choices sound similar, but only one can sit in front of a noun to show ownership.
hints.S01_C6: The ones showing the class how to plant are the TWO GARDENERS - more than one person, and the pronoun begins the sentence. Ask: which pronoun is the SUBJECT form for several other people? Not the form that comes after a verb.
hints.S01_C7: '___ all tried it and got OUR hands dirty' - the word OUR tells you exactly who this is. Ask: which pronoun is the SUBJECT form for me and my classmates together? Not the object form used after a verb.
hints.S01_C8: They GAVE a card to MS TAN - one woman, receiving the card. Ask: which pronoun for one female goes after a verb, in the object position? The subject form 'she' cannot receive anything.
hints.S01_D1: She was able to READ THE NAME 'Amy' on the side, so she must have taken her time looking. Ask: does the blank describe HOW she looked? Then it needs an adverb - and which one fits looking closely, not rushing?
hints.S01_D2: Amy 'was looking EVERYWHERE for it' and the bottle turned up by the school GATE. Ask: what happened to Amy's bottle before Mei found it? The blank follows 'had', so a past form is needed.
hints.S01_D3: Mei wanted the bottle handed in to the OFFICE without delay - the blank tells you HOW she walked. Ask: which adverb describes moving fast? The other -ly word describes doing something with great care.
hints.S01_D4: The teacher praises her, Amy thanks her, and Mei HELPED a classmate. Ask: how does that feel? Choose the feeling word that matches a good outcome - not the one for anger and not the one for regret.
hints.S01_D5: The bottle was handed in at the OFFICE, and now Amy is getting it back. Ask: which past verb means to give something back to its owner? Not the word for letting it fall by accident.
hints.S01_E1: The underlined word is a describing word, but here it must describe HOW they sit - 'sit ___ and not MAKE ANY NOISE'. Ask: which ending turns a describing word into one that describes an action?
hints.S01_E2: WRITE is an irregular verb, so it cannot take -ed. Ask: how would you say it in the past - 'yesterday he ___ his name'? Irregular verbs change their shape instead of adding an ending.
hints.S01_E3: 'He LOOKED very ___' needs a describing word for how Sam felt, not the plain verb. Ask: which ending turns this verb into a feeling that describes a person, like 'excited' or 'tired'?
hints.S01_E4: The VOICES belong to the students - more than one student. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or does it only make a plural? Where does the apostrophe go when the owners are many?
hints.S01_E5: The PAPERS belong to the students being spoken to. Ask: does the underlined spelling mean 'at that place', or 'belonging to them'? They sound the same, so decide by meaning, not by sound.
hints.S01_F1: A yes/no question turned into REPORTED speech. Ask three things: which small joining word follows ASKED? Does the question keep its question word order, or become normal statement order? And what happens to 'you' and to 'have'?
hints.S01_F2: BOTH Tom and his sister means TWO people, so the subject is now plural. Ask: does a plural subject keep the -s on the verb, or drop it? Say 'drawing' only once - the second sentence adds nothing new.
